Applications without those route rules and without experimental.early404, fully prerendered applications, and client-only applications are unaffected; the impact is limited to availability. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.

GLPI is a free asset and IT management software package. From 9.5.0 until 10.0.27 and 11.0.9, authenticated users could access ITIL followups, tasks, or solutions generated from templates without a read-permission check on the parent ticket, problem, or change. Depending on the template configuration, this could reveal information from parent items the user could not otherwise read. This issue is fixed in versions 10.0.27 and 11.0.9.

paicoding 1.0.0 through 1.0.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in image upload because ImageServiceImpl.validateStaticImg accepts SVG files, which are then served from the site origin when local storage is used. Authenticated attackers can upload script-bearing SVG images that execute when victims view them, stealing the non-HttpOnly f-session cookie to hijack accounts.

paicoding 1.0.3 contains a payment bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to unlock paid articles by guessing weak payment confirmation codes. Attackers can start a payment, enumerate roughly 2000 IdUtil.genPayCode counter values, and submit the matching verifyCode to the unauthenticated callback to mark it paid.

SurveyKing 1.13.0 through 1.13.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the server accepts a respondent-supplied survey snapshot and the frontend renders its titles via innerHTML. Anonymous respondents can submit a forged snapshot embedding event handlers such as img onerror that execute in an administrator's browser session when the response is viewed.

ragent 1.1.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject scripts by uploading SVG knowledge-base documents served inline as image/svg+xml. Attackers can upload a script-bearing SVG via /knowledge-base/{kb-id}/docs/upload so that victims opening /knowledge-base/docs/{docId}/file execute it in the application origin, enabling account takeover.

Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered users to run script by uploading HTML files served inline as text/html. Attackers can send a victim the /api/file/stream/preview/{fileId} link to execute script in the application origin, calling /apis endpoints to expose the victim's files and account.

Seafile SeaDoc converter 2.0.4 before 2.0.11 and 3.0.0 before 3.0.8 contains an absolute path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers holding a public share token to execute code. Attackers supply an absolute filename to /api/v1/confluence-to-wiki/ to extract a ZIP from download_url into the Python library path, then trigger the module's import via a file-convert request.

NginxPulse 1.5.0 before 1.6.26 contains an unauthenticated sql injection vulnerability that allows remote attackers to append SQL via the id and locationType parameters of /api/stats/:type. Attackers can close the quoted table-name identifier and use error-based output to read database contents, and read or write server files via PostgreSQL superuser functions.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, and 1.6.1, bws_srv_start() in ports/linux/websocket-srv.c builds the libwebsockets server context with a CA certificate loaded but never sets LWS_SERVER_OPTION_REQUIRE_VALID_OPENSSL_CLIENT_CERT, so the hub accepts TLS connections from clients presenting no certificate at all. Any network-reachable host can join the BACnet/SC mesh without credentials. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, 1.6.1, and 1.7.0.

AutoMapper is a convention-based object-object mapper in .NET. Prior to 15.1.4 and from 16.0.0 until 16.3.0, AutoMapper can recurse without an effective MaxDepth limit when mapping polymorphic graphs through Include or IncludeBase, runtime-typed object or interface members, nested Dictionary<string, object> or ExpandoObject sources, or recursive ConvertUsing type converters. Deep attacker-influenced graphs on these paths can throw an uncatchable StackOverflowException and terminate the process. This issue is fixed in versions 15.1.4 and 16.3.0.

sqlite3 provides Ruby bindings for the SQLite3 embedded database. Prior to 2.10.2, sqlite3-ruby casts Ruby string lengths to int before passing SQL through Database#prepare, bound String or Blob values through Statement#bind_param, and String or Blob results from Ruby-defined SQL functions and aggregates through Database#create_function and Database#create_aggregate. On 64-bit platforms, a string of 4 GiB (2^32 bytes) or larger can wrap the length so SQLite processes only a prefix. A truncated SQL string can drop trailing clauses such as a WHERE condition, while a truncated bound value matters only when the application validated the full value before binding it. Exploitation requires the application and server to accept and retain the unusually large attacker-controlled string. If a dropped SQL clause contained a bind placeholder, binding raises SQLite3::RangeException instead of running the query. This issue is fixed in version 2.10.2.

russh is a Rust SSH client and server library that includes an SSH agent protocol implementation. Prior to version 0.65.1, try_sign() captures an Arc<PrivateKey> before awaiting Agent::confirm() and does not revalidate the shared lock state or key presence after the await. This is a distinct residual defect in the remediation for CVE-2026-116794. A peer, including a remote SSH server using agent forwarding, can begin a confirmation-constrained signature request while the agent is unlocked and receive the signature after another connection locks the agent if the stale confirmation returns true. New post-lock requests are rejected and private key material is not disclosed, but the pending operation bypasses the current lock state. This issue is fixed in version 0.65.1.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, the BACnet FILE object implementation allows remote WriteProperty(PROP_FILE_SIZE) requests to change the size of a stream-access FILE object without checking whether that FILE is marked Read_Only. When the FILE backend is RAMFS, enlarging the file only performs realloc() and updates the stored size; the newly exposed tail region is not initialized before later reads. As a result, a remote client can enlarge a read-only RAMFS-backed stream-access FILE and then immediately retrieve the newly exposed region with AtomicReadFile(stream-access). Depending on the allocator and build configuration, the returned data may contain sanitizer fill bytes, stale heap contents, or other unintended process memory. Shrinking the file through the same path can also remotely truncate content that was intended to be read-only. This issue has been patched in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.

bit-vec is a compact vector of bits. Prior to version 0.10.0, there is undefined behavior if a user performs deserialize from an untrusted source and unsafe get_unchecked. A user of this library may be impacted by incorrect behavior if they perform deserialize from an untrusted source and run operations on the deserialized BitVec. This issue has been patched in version 0.10.0.

Kanbanz by Softaculous plugin for WordPress before 1.0.3 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows authenticated Kanban Staff users to access and modify boards they are not members of by exploiting admin-ajax handlers that fail to call kanbanz_user_can_access_board() or per-task edit checks on attacker-supplied board_id or task_id parameters. Attackers can supply arbitrary board IDs to read sensitive task data, overwrite status columns, subtasks, and labels, inject comments, upload or delete attachments, and create tasks or set WIP limits on boards owned by other teams.

SvelteKit is a framework for rapidly developing robust, performant web applications using Svelte. Prior to versions 2.70.4 and 3.1.1, apps configured with router.resolution: 'server' could treat a pathname beginning with // as a protocol-relative module specifier during client-side navigation. A socially engineered link could therefore make server-side route resolution import and execute JavaScript from another origin in the user's browser. This issue is fixed in 2.70.4 and 3.1.1.

SvelteKit is a framework for rapidly developing robust, performant web applications using Svelte. From version 2.42.0 until 3.1.1, applications using the experimental remote functions flag and a remote form function could perform quadratic synchronous work while parsing a specially crafted request with many form entries. The parsing work could block the event loop for an extended period and deny service. This issue is fixed in 3.1.1.

Post to Google My Business plugin for WordPress before 3.5.7 contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users with Contributor-level privileges or higher to make the server send requests to arbitrary hosts by supplying an unvalidated mbp_post_attachment URL that reaches a raw getimagesize() call in validate_external_image_size() via the preview REST route. Attackers can exploit this to perform internal port scanning, probe internal-only services and cloud metadata endpoints, and trigger GET-based side effects on internal systems, bypassing network perimeter controls since the request originates from the web server.

affectedData.product: Post to Google My Business (Google Business Profile)

descriptions.value: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, Application.add_domain() converts every asterisk wildcard in a domain mask into a greedy regular-expression fragment, so a mask containing two or more wildcards can take polynomial time to reject a long Host header that does not match. A remote attacker can repeatedly send such headers to a server configured with a multi-wildcard domain mask and stall the event loop. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, the C WebSocket reader adds a declared frame length to the size of an already buffered partial message using signed 64-bit arithmetic. A length near two to the power of 63 can overflow, allowing the max_msg_size check to pass. A remote peer can send a small non-final fragment followed by an oversized message and cause unbounded memory consumption. The Python WebSocket reader is unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, the WebSocket reader continues parsing frames already received after the receive queue pauses the transport, and empty messages are not counted toward the queue size. With permessage-deflate, one read of compressed frames can add many megabytes of decompressed messages to the receive queue. A remote peer can send many small or compressed messages faster than the application consumes them and cause excessive memory use in a server or client. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.
IBM App Connect Operator and IBM App Connect Enterprise Certified Containers Operands is vulnerable to Log Forging on a request to create a resource.

affectedData.product: App Connect Enterprise Certified Containers Operands

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in dbus when configured with the nonce-tcp transport. An unauthenticated attacker able to connect to an exposed listener can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by opening a connection and withholding the expected authentication token. Because the server processes this verification without enforcing a timeout, the stalled connection blocks the accept process and prevents legitimate clients from establishing new connections.

A security flaw has been discovered in Stirling-Tools Stirling-PDF up to 3.3.0. Affected is the function WorkflowParticipantController.getParticipantDetails of the file app/proprietary/src/main/java/stirling/software/proprietary/workflow/controller/WorkflowParticipantController.java of the component Participant Details Endpoint. Performing a manipulation results in insufficient session timeout value. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

PrestaShop before 8.2.9 and 9.2.1 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows an authenticated Webservice API key holder to read and modify customer records belonging to any shop in a multi-shop installation. Attackers can exploit the missing record-level shop ownership check in shopHasRight() and saveEntityFromXml() to read sensitive customer data such as password hashes and secure keys, and change a customer's email and password via create, update, and delete requests, resulting in account takeover.

A weakness has been identified in Akaunting up to 3.3.0. The affected element is the function calculation_to_quantity of the file helpers.php of the component Invoice Item Validation. Executing a manipulation of the argument quantity can lead to numeric range comparison without minimum check. The attack may be performed from remote. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was identified in CoolerMaster MASTERPLUS+ 1.9.6. This affects the function sub_11504 in the library WinRing0x64.sys of the component Device Driver. The manipulation of the argument PhysicalAddress leads to incorrect default permissions. The attack can only be performed from a local environment. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Pulse from 5.0.17 before 6.8.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the /api/ai/approvals endpoints that allows authenticated viewer-level users to manage approval requests. Attackers can list pending requests to expose proposed commands and targets, and approve or deny other users' requests, altering decision and audit state.

Ettercap through 0.8.5.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dissector_mountd() in src/dissectors/ec_mountd.c that validates RPC credential and directory lengths independently rather than against the packet end. Network-adjacent attackers can send a crafted MOUNT MNT call to read up to 100 bytes past the heap buffer, leaking memory to the console and logs.

A vulnerability was found in Kingston FURY CTRL RGB Control Software up to 2.0.66.0. The impacted element is an unknown function in the library NTIOLib_X64.sys of the component IOCTL Handler. Performing a manipulation results in exposed ioctl with insufficient access control. The attack is only possible with local access.

A security vulnerability has been detected in TRENDnet TEW-657BRM 1.00.1. This vulnerability affects the function sprintf of the file /setup.cgi of the component mini_httpd. Such manipulation leads to out-of-bounds write. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The vendor explains: ""I am not able to confirm if such vulnerability exists as the product has been EOL for more than 15 years. We will send out an announcement letting customers know." This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

A vulnerability has been found in sigoden dufs up to 0.46.0. This affects an unknown part of the file src/server.rs of the component WebDAV COPY Operation Handler. The manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. Upgrading to version 0.47.0 is able to mitigate this issue. The identifier of the patch is fba13dffb9c65b5e5e26419f64de709200277a04. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component.

Zr.Admin.NET commit e6ceaf4 through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in FrontArticleController that allows authenticated users to change other users' article visibility and pin state. Attackers can send PUT /front/article/changePublic with their own UserId in the body to make private articles public, then read them anonymously via GET /front/article/{id}.

A security flaw has been discovered in Linux Foundation Magma up to 1.9.0. The affected element is an unknown function of the file orc8r/lib/go/registry/interceptors.go. Performing a manipulation results in hard-coded credentials. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A security flaw has been discovered in D-Link DIR-850L FW1.20WWb03. This impacts an unknown function of the file /usr/sbin/consolepwd of the component Console Login. Performing a manipulation results in hard-coded credentials. The attack requires a local approach. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.

A flaw has been found in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6. This affects the function app_guest_export of the file /cgi-bin/mainfunction.cgi. This manipulation of the argument filename causes path traversal. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 is able to mitigate this issue. The affected component should be upgraded. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."

A vulnerability has been found in DrayTek Vigor2960 1.5.1.6. This vulnerability affects the function set_table of the file /cgi-bin/mainfunction.cgi. Such manipulation of the argument jsondata leads to command injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 is able to resolve this issue. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."

GeoPulse 1.5.0 through 2.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /api/v1/places/geocoding/{id} that allows authenticated users to read other users' private locations. Attackers can enumerate sequential reverse_geocoding_location ids to retrieve other users' custom place names, city, country, coordinates and bounding boxes from their history.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in glTFCommon::Util::ParseDataURI caused by storing the data offset in a signed char. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF file with a raw data URI whose segment starts beyond byte 127 to crash applications or leak adjacent heap memory.

Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SRP server mechanism because srp_server_mech_step2 does not reject client public values A that are multiples of N. Unauthenticated network clients can send A equal to N to force a zero shared secret, authenticating as any existing user without the password and learning session keys.

littlefs through 2.11.3, when built with LFS_MIGRATE, contains a type confusion vulnerability in lfs_dir_traverse() that treats a stack lfs_diskoff struct as an lfs_attr array. Attackers can supply a crafted littlefs v1 image whose metadata is read as LFS_FROM_USERATTRS during migration, causing out-of-bounds stack reads and process crashes.

CloudPaste 1.1.0 through 1.9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain WebDAV storage credentials through the unauthenticated /api/proxy/link endpoint. Attackers who know a public share slug can retrieve the Basic Authorization header containing the WebDAV username and password, then read, modify, or delete files on the WebDAV server.

Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to modify any account via the /kal-api/auth/user/edit endpoint. Attackers holding only read permission can set their admin flag and 'all' permission or reset an administrator's password to fully take over the instance.

Tensei through 0.11.5 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in the @tensei/media plugin that allows unauthenticated attackers to upload dangerous file types via the files/upload route. Attackers can set the multipart Content-Type to upload HTML or SVG files served from the application origin, causing stored cross-site scripting and storage consumption.

Tensei through 0.11.5 contains an open redirect vulnerability in the @tensei/social-auth SocialAuthCallbackController that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by supplying an unvalidated clientCallback query parameter. Attackers can craft links to the /:provider/callback route that send victims to attacker-controlled sites for phishing and leak the issued temporary access token appended after login.

SeaweedFS before 4.42 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to probe local files by supplying a filesystem path in gcs_google_application_credentials. Attackers can send crafted gRPC FetchAndWriteNeedle requests and use differing error messages to learn file existence, readability, and partial content shape on the host.

wallabag 2.3.3 before 2.6.16 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through article author metadata rendered with Twig raw in entry.html.twig. Attackers can embed HTML event handlers in a web page's author metadata so scripts run in a victim's wallabag session when the saved entry is opened, exposing their data.

Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.7 contain a reachable assertion vulnerability in ParsePFDEntry() that allows attackers to abort applications via an invalid orientation tag. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file with an out-of-range WMP_tagTransformation value to crash applications using default assertion-enabled builds, or store an unchecked orientation value otherwise.

Frappe CRM before 1.84.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the get_deal_contacts method that allows authenticated low-privileged users to read contacts of deals they cannot access. Attackers can supply or iterate CRM Deal names to obtain linked contacts' full names, email addresses, and mobile numbers, bypassing row-level permission rules.

Rocboss paopao-ce through 0.6.0-alpha.3 fails to validate the attachment_price field when creating posts, allowing authenticated users to set negative prices on charge attachments. Attackers with two ordinary accounts can download the attachment via GET /v1/attachment, where the negative price increases the buyer's wallet balance, minting funds to purchase other users' paid attachments.

REBUILD 2.7.0 through 4.5.4 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to inject AjQL conditions through the plan parameter of /project/tasks/list. Attackers can use priority-* plans and the returned task count as a boolean oracle to recover a task creator's SHA-256 password hash and log in as that user, including the administrator.

OfficeCLI 1.0.56 through 1.0.161 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the officecli watch preview that allows attackers to inject script via unescaped numbering w:color values. Attackers can craft a DOCX whose color closes the style element, then abuse the unauthenticated /api/batch endpoint to read local files and modify the watched document.

DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.5 through 3.8.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows registered users to leak server-wide GitLab or Gitea tokens via repository_url. Attackers can create a gitlab or gitea project pointing to a controlled host and request its branches to capture the operator's token and reach internal hosts.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the fetchClientSecret Next.js server action that allows unauthenticated attackers to create Stripe checkout sessions for other teams. Attackers can invoke the action with a forged Team object containing a victim's stripeCustomerId to obtain Growth plan Checkout session client secrets with attacker-influenced return URLs.

Cetmix Tower through 17.0.3.0.0 and 18.0 before 18.0.4.0.1 contains an improper SSH host key verification vulnerability in SSHConnection.connect() that falls back to Paramiko's AutoAddPolicy when no host key is pinned. On-path attackers using ARP or DNS spoofing can present their own host key during Skip Host Key or Get from Host connections to capture stored SSH passwords and tamper with commands and files.

Prime CMS (@primecms/core) through 0.4.0-beta.0 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the updateSystem GraphQL mutation that allows authenticated administrators to execute shell commands via the package version string. Attackers can append shell metacharacters to the unvalidated version value, which is passed to child_process.exec() in yarn add or npm install commands, executing commands as the server process.

Contentlayer @contentlayer/core through 0.3.4 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject JavaScript by embedding single quotes in content file names. Attackers can add a content file whose name breaks out of the import specifier in makeDataExportFile(), executing injected code when contentlayer dev or a Next.js dev server imports the generated module.

Rowy through 3.0.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table write access to inject scripts via URL field links lacking scheme validation. Attackers can store values like javascript: URIs containing the string http in URL cells, executing script when victims click the open-link button to steal Firebase sessions.

NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain administrator access by using the hardcoded default password 'root'. Attackers can send base64-encoded 'root' to POST /admin/login when NP_ADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD is unset to obtain admin tokens and fully control the site.

qbee-agent is the device agent component of the qbee.io IoT device management platform. Prior to 2026.41, the unpackTar extraction logic in app/utils/tar.go validates cleaned archive entry paths with strings.HasPrefix(targetPath, destdirClean) without enforcing a path-separator boundary. When UseContext enables the Docker Compose build context path in app/configuration/bundle_docker_compose.go, a less-privileged archive supplier with delegated configuration and/or file-manager access can provide a sibling-prefix traversal entry that passes the check, causing utils.UnpackTar to create directories and regular files outside the intended context extraction directory with qbee-agent process privileges, despite the supplier lacking authority to write those sibling files. In deployments where only full device or fleet administrators can provide Docker Compose context archives, this behavior is hardening rather than a crossed security boundary. The demonstrated impact is limited to nearby cache or project paths sharing the destination prefix, may affect integrity or availability of qbee-agent-managed Docker Compose state, and does not establish arbitrary absolute-path writes or direct code execution. This issue is fixed in version 2026.41.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, a user with CMS_ACCESS_SecurityAdmin but without ADMIN can edit or reparent a group that grants ADMIN-equivalent permissions through an assigned role or a parent group, thereby escalating to full administrative privileges. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. From 3.8.0 until 4.6.0, the write_attachments() and write_sample() APIs use attacker-controlled attachment filenames without sufficient sanitization and path containment validation. Directory traversal sequences and absolute filesystem paths can cause an attachment to be written outside the intended output directory. An attacker can overwrite files accessible to the parsing process when an application extracts attachments from a crafted message. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.0.

mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. From 4.6.0 until 4.6.3, write_attachments() calls _safe_attachment_filename() and write_sample() without isolating failures for individual attacker-controlled MIME parts. An RFC 2231 filename containing a NUL, a basename exceeding NAME_MAX, or an undecodable base64 payload can raise ValueError, OSError, or binascii.Error and abort the entire save loop. Later attachments remain unwritten; when a caller catches only MailParserError, the failure is not surfaced through the expected library-exception path. If a downstream scanner or sandbox reads only the extraction directory, a payload after the crafted part can be missed even though it remains in the delivered message, and the aborted batch also causes availability loss. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.3.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 15.0.0 until 15.5.29 and 16.4.5, the /_next/image optimizer in self-hosted Next.js deployments can process attacker-supplied SVG content even when dangerouslyAllowSVG is false, which is the default. The SVG reaches a parser that the application intended to keep disabled, increasing exposure to denial of service and vulnerabilities in SVG decoding. This issue is fixed in versions 16.4.5 and 15.5.29.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. Prior to 15.5.29 and 16.4.5, self-hosted Next.js App Router route handlers and the fetch cache that return a fetched upstream response unchanged can emit a response whose declared framing does not match the body actually sent. When the application is behind an HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy that permits pipelined response queueing, a crafted upstream response can desynchronize responses between clients. The resulting desynchronization can inject a response into another client's queue or disclose another client's response. This issue is fixed in versions 16.4.5 and 15.5.29.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.2.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js applications with Cache Components enabled can reuse an outer 'use cache' entry across root param values when a nested 'use cache' call reads a root param through next/root-params and returns a value containing pending promises. React Flight can deliver the ready portion to the outer function before the inner cache finishes publishing its root-param dependencies. The outer entry can then complete and be persisted under a key that omits the root param, causing the first written value to be served for other root param values and allowing the outer entry to ignore nested cache tag invalidation and lifetimes. The leaked value is not attacker controlled and depends on which invocation writes the entry first. This variant does not require an existing inner cache entry or a slow cache handler and is not covered by the fix for CVE-2026-103004. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.3.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js applications using the same 'use cache' function directly during rendering and through unstable_cache() can disclose cached data across root params when that function reads a root param. During the first fill after a cold process start, cross-request deduplication allows a concurrent unstable_cache() request to join the direct call's in-flight fill and receive its result before the root param mismatch is rejected. unstable_cache() then persists that result under a key that omits root params, causing later requests for other root param values to receive the same entry until revalidation or eviction. Exploitation requires the unstable_cache() request to arrive while the first fill is in flight. Outside this race, nesting 'use cache' inside unstable_cache() raises an unsupported-operation error, and avoiding that nesting prevents the issue. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

Axigen Mail Server 10.3.3.67 through 10.3.3.x, 10.4.42 through 10.4.x, 10.5.29 through 10.5.x, 10.6.x before 10.6.41, and 10.7.x before 10.7.3 contains an unauthenticated denial of service vulnerability caused by uncontrolled recursion when validating query parameter and cookie values with a recursive regular expression engine before authentication in the WebAdmin and WebMail services. Attackers can send a single HTTP request with a query parameter or cookie value of a few thousand characters to exhaust the worker thread stack and crash the server process, taking down SMTP, IMAP, POP3, and web services repeatedly.

VB-Audio VB-CABLE before 3.5.2.0 contains out-of-bounds read and write vulnerabilities in the vbaudio_cable64_win10.sys kernel streaming driver's KSPROPSETID_Audio MUTE, VOLUMELEVEL, and PEAKMETER2 property handlers that allow a local standard user to supply an all-channels sentinel value improperly used as a loop terminator or array index instead of being bounds-checked. Attackers can exploit the accessible low-integrity KS filter device object to write attacker-controlled values sequentially into kernel memory, corrupting kernel globals and object pointers, or read past an array boundary to leak kernel memory, resulting in local privilege escalation or denial of service via a kernel bug check.
Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office OneNote allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 3.5.0 until 3.13.0, built-in penetration-detection patterns in guard_core/handlers/suspatterns_handler.py execute through a direct pattern.search(content) call instead of the timeout-protected create_safe_matcher() path used for custom patterns. The built-in template-injection detector contains an unbounded expression with quadratic behavior when scanning repeated opening braces. Because penetration detection and enhanced mode are enabled by a stock SecurityConfig, an unauthenticated request can block the shared asyncio event loop, affecting all application endpoints. The triggering input does not produce a detection match, so the request can complete without incrementing ban counters or being recorded as suspicious. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 1.0.0 until 3.13.0, _extract_from_forwarded_header() in guard_core/utils.py returns the selected X-Forwarded-For entry without validating that it is an IP address. In deployments configured with trusted_proxies where the selected entry is attacker-controlled, the arbitrary client_ip string reaches BehaviorTracker in guard_core/handlers/behavior_handler.py and is interpolated into Redis key names and blocking KEYS glob patterns. Glob metacharacters can cause one request to count other clients' behavior events, embedded separators can disturb key parsing, and rotating identities can create unbounded keys while repeatedly scanning the shared Redis keyspace. A non-IP identity can also reach a ban action and cause an uncaught validation error. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

EGroupware is a web-based groupware server written in PHP. Prior to 23.1.20260601 and 26.5.20260507, the processURL2InlineImages logic in api/src/Mail.php treats non-HTTP image sources in an HTML mail body as local paths and passes a decoded attacker-controlled file:// URI to file_get_contents. Any authenticated user with mail access can cause files readable by the web server process to be embedded as inline MIME attachments in outgoing email, exposing local configuration, credentials, private keys, or other server files. This issue is fixed in versions 23.1.20260601 and 26.5.20260507.

qbee-agent is the device agent component of the qbee.io IoT device management platform. Prior to 2026.27, the privileged createFile helper followed attacker-controlled symbolic links during file creation. A local unprivileged user whose account is managed by the SSH Keys bundle could replace ~/.ssh with a link to /root/.ssh, causing the agent to write an authorized key for root. On systems using RAUC download mode with ineffective kernel symlink protection, the predictable /tmp/.bundle.raucb.part path could be linked to a system file and then overwritten or truncated during an update. A file-distribution destination beneath an attacker-controlled directory could similarly redirect the partial-download path so the agent changed ownership of a sensitive file. These vectors could result in root privilege escalation, arbitrary file modification, or denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 2026.27.

containerd is an open-source container runtime. From 2.2.0 until 2.2.10, 2.3.7, and 2.4.2, image manifest processing through the transfer service can encounter a child descriptor containing the io.containerd.manifest.subject annotation and a malformed digest. Pulling or importing such an image, including through a default CRI PullImage request, can trigger an unrecovered panic and crash the containerd daemon. In Kubernetes, kubelet retries can repeatedly trigger the crash and disrupt container operations on the worker node. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.10, 2.3.7, and 2.4.2.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. In 7.260722.0 and earlier, a user with the SETTINGS_SETCUSTOMIZATION capability can configure a webhook notifier with an arbitrary destination URL and invoke notifierTest to make the OpenCTI server send the request immediately. The request can target internal services or cloud metadata endpoints that are reachable from the server, enabling server-side request forgery without waiting for a notifier event. No fixed release is verified by the available evidence; later releases remain unclassified.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260428.0, the token GraphQL mutation used for primary login has no endpoint-specific rate limit, while the global Express limiter defaults to permitting 10,000 requests in a one-second window. An unauthenticated remote attacker can make password guesses at network speed against a chosen user account and, if a credential is recovered, access the account's threat-intelligence data and permitted operations. This issue is fixed in version 7.260428.0.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260513.0, Draft Workspace identifiers are accepted without verifying that the authenticated user can access the referenced draft. Any authenticated user can enumerate draftWorkspaces, use a disclosed DRAFT_ID with draftWorkspaceEntities to read unpublished reports, descriptions, observables, and other staged intelligence, or place the identifier in the opencti-draft-id header and run mutations that inject entities and relationships into another user's private workspace. The flaw permits cross-user disclosure and tampering but does not cause a denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 7.260513.0.

GLPI is a free asset and IT management software package. Prior to 10.0.28, 11.0.10, and 12.0.1, authenticated users can craft a URL that invokes massive actions without all required object- and action-specific authorization checks. The bypass permits operations outside the user's granted rights, including unauthorized plugin activation, deactivation, and uninstallation for plugins already present on the filesystem and other state-changing maintenance actions. This issue is fixed in versions 10.0.28, 11.0.10, and 12.0.1.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260624.0, an Organization Administrator with VIRTUAL_ORGANIZATION_ADMIN and KNOWLEDGE_KNUPDATE can use organizationFieldPatch to replace the administered organization's grantable_groups without a SETTINGS_SETACCESSES authorization check. The administrator can add the built-in Administrators group to that grant scope and then bypass the grantable_groups guard added by the incomplete CVE-2026-44730 remediation to add their own account to Administrators. Membership grants the BYPASS capability after session cache refresh, escalating the tenant-scoped account to global administrator with access across organizations, users, settings, markings, connectors, and ingestion. This issue is fixed in version 7.260624.0.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260706.0, the logsWorkerConfig GraphQL query is authorized with the broad CONNECTORAPI capability and returns Elasticsearch connection details including elasticsearch_username, elasticsearch_password, elasticsearch_api_key, the URL, index, proxy, and TLS-verification setting. A holder of any connector API bearer token can retrieve this credential material. If the returned credentials are valid and Elasticsearch is reachable, the caller can directly read, modify, or delete OpenCTI indices and audit history outside application-layer role, marking, organization, and audit controls, with the practical impact bounded by the credentials' privileges and network reachability. This issue is fixed in version 7.260706.0.

iSponsorBlockTV is a SponsorBlock client for YouTube TV clients. Prior to 2.11.0, src/iSponsorBlockTV/dial_client.py trusts the SSDP LOCATION URL supplied by a local-network responder without validating its destination. During automatic discovery, this can cause an attacker-directed GET request and a constrained POST request to a path ending in /YouTube; the POST uses application-defined headers and an application-defined payload rather than attacker-selected request contents. The requests can reach internal services, but the detailed request behavior states that response data and errors are not returned to the attacker, making the demonstrated behavior blind SSRF with bounded integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 2.11.0.

GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a use of uninitialized memory vulnerability in stbl_AddCTS() that allows attackers to corrupt sample table data via crafted MP4 files. Attackers can supply an MP4 with out-of-order composition time offsets for MP4Box import, triggering invalid memory access in gf_list_get() and crashing the process.

Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js. Prior to 2.5.315, an authenticated user with write:pages can store JavaScript expressions in the v-slot:tabs or v-slot:content attributes of page HTML because server/modules/rendering/html-security/renderer.js adds those executable Vue directives to DOMPurify's allowlist. The sanitized output is inserted as rendered page HTML and later compiled by the Vue 2 runtime compiler, so the expressions execute in the Wiki.js origin when another user views the page even when the author lacks write:scripts and administrative permissions. The script runs with the viewer's browser session and can read same-origin data, modify displayed content, present phishing content, or perform actions available to that viewer, including privileged GraphQL operations when a privileged user opens the page. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.315.

7-Zip File Manager before 26.03 fails to detect archive entry names padded with Unicode space characters, allowing attackers to bypass the deceptive file name warning in CPanel::IsVirus_Message. Attackers can craft archive entries like a PDF name followed by ideographic spaces and .hta to hide the real extension, executing script content via ShellExecuteExW when opened.

Umbraco CMS 17.0.0 before 17.7.1 and 18.0.0 before 18.2.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in Management API document version endpoints that skip per-document ContentPermissionByResource checks. Authenticated back-office users restricted to a start node can list and read document versions outside their tree by GUID, exposing unpublished values and altering prevent-cleanup flags.

TridotsTech go1cms master branch through commit 7f68d05 and version-3 branch before commit ead8da3 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the guest-whitelisted update_doc method that allows unauthenticated attackers to modify any document. Attackers can supply a doctype, name and arbitrary fields that are saved with ignore_permissions=True, altering User records to escalate privileges, take over accounts or tamper with business data.

Cloud Commander (cloudcmd) before 19.21.4 contains an authentication bypass and path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to rename files by sending PUT /rename requests handled before authentication middleware. Attackers can supply absolute or ../ paths in the from and to arrays to move any file the Node.js process can access outside the configured root, causing data loss or denial of service.

SplitPro through 2.1.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the addOrEditExpense and addOrEditCurrencyConversion tRPC mutations that allows authenticated users to assign expenses to arbitrary users. Attackers can enumerate sequential user IDs and supply them in participants or paidBy fields to fabricate debts on victims' balances, even in unseen groups.

crw-server before 0.45.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to reach internal services by supplying an unvalidated baseUrl to the /v1/scrape endpoint. Attackers can set llmApiKey and request the summary format, making the server POST to loopback or private addresses and use returned warnings as a reachability oracle.

B3log Solo through 4.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject script by setting a malicious article title rendered without escaping. Attackers can set titles, including via the B3 sync endpoint, so admin/article-pwd.ftl, skin templates, and js/page.js article lists execute script in visitors' and administrators' browsers.

B3log Solo through 4.4.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the console article update API that allows authenticated authors to inject SQL through unvalidated JSON property names. Attackers can send a PUT request to /console/article/ with crafted property names used as UPDATE column names, then read query results back through the updated article.

BookStack before 26.09.2 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the ZIP content importer that allows authenticated users with the Import Content permission to exhaust server storage. Attackers can upload a small ZIP whose data.json references one bundled file many times, causing ZipImportRunner::importAttachment() to write a full copy per reference.

Chyrp Lite (xenocrat/chyrp-lite) contains a missing brute-force protection vulnerability in the main_login() function that allows remote attackers to repeatedly submit login attempts against the admin account without any attempt counter, lockout, delay, or CAPTCHA enforcement. Attackers can send unlimited password guesses via POST requests to the login action until a correct credential is found, gaining full administrative control including post publishing, user management, and file uploads.

The Coder VS Code extension opens Coder workspaces in VS Code with a single click. From 0.1.20 until 1.14.6, a malicious repository can provide .vscode/settings.json values for security-sensitive Coder settings because the extension permits workspace and folder scope to override those settings. Values such as coder.headerCommand and coder.tlsCertRefreshCommand are later executed as shell commands, while other affected settings can redirect the Coder CLI binary or download source, inject CLI or SSH flags, replace TLS material, disable TLS verification, or change identity and credential-storage behavior. A victim with the extension installed must open the malicious workspace or repository; when the extension activates, attacker-controlled commands can run with the victim user's privileges. The issue also affects untrusted workspaces because the extension declares untrusted-workspace support without preventing consumption of the workspace-controlled settings. This issue is fixed in version 1.14.6.

In Open Object Rexx (ooRexx) before 5.2.0, RXAPI relies on a world-writable /tmp file unless XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is set, or localhost TCP port 10010, allowing RXAPI communication by any local user, e.g., for injection of a macro that will be executed by a REXX script.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a stored sql injection vulnerability in the MySQL driver that allows database users with table creation rights to inject SQL through unescaped geometry column names in unconvert_field(). Attackers can craft a column name containing an SQL expression that executes with another AdminNeo user's privileges when they edit a row, save it, or export the table.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered users to inject javascript: links via FAQ comments. When the comment editor is enabled, Utils::parseUrl() strips https:// from sanitized hrefs, turning an allowed https://javascript:443/ link into executable script that runs on the shared admin origin when clicked.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an improper reference counting flaw on multisite deployments, allowing editors to delete other instances' attachment files. Because linkedRecords() counts only the local faqattachment table, deleting an attachment with shared md5 content makes File::delete() unlink the shared blob, destroying another instance's files.

phpMyFAQ 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated frontend users to receive restricted FAQ titles by subscribing to Web Push notifications. When editors publish user/group-restricted FAQs, WebPushService::sendToAll() delivers the question, FAQ id, category, and slugified URL to every subscriber, bypassing the FAQ ACL.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains an sql injection vulnerability in the ClickHouse driver because idf_escape() doubles backticks but does not escape backslashes in identifiers. Attackers can lure a logged-in user into opening a GET link with a column name ending in a backslash in columns, where, or order parameters, causing query text to be parsed as SQL.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows category- or language-restricted editors to bypass scoped rights via public REST write endpoints. Attackers with a scoped right and the shared API token can use PUT faq/update, POST faq/create, and POST category to rewrite published FAQs and create root categories outside their scope.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows delegated group or user admins to remove rights they do not hold by submitting empty rights lists. Attackers can send an empty rightIds or userRights array to group/permissions or user/update-rights to wipe all rights of more-privileged groups or administrators.

phpMyFAQ before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in its public FAQ REST API that exposes author names and e-mail addresses to unauthenticated callers. Attackers can query the faq and paginated faqs endpoints to bulk-harvest e-mails and de-anonymise users who opted out of GDPR author visibility.

phpMyFAQ 4.1.0 before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in POST /api/webauthn/prepare that creates accounts as active, bypassing manual activation and domain whitelisting. Anonymous attackers can obtain the freely issued CSRF token and register an activated account with an unverified email to access registered-user-only content and functions.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in updateUserRights that lets USER_EDIT admins drop category restrictions on group rights. Attackers can re-save rights through the user update-rights API to convert category-restricted group rights into global direct rights, then edit, publish or delete FAQs in withheld categories.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the ClaudeSqlPlugin, GeminiSqlPlugin, and OpenWebUiPlugin sendHeaders() handlers that run on the login page. Unauthenticated attackers can POST claude, gemini, or openwebui fields to relay arbitrary prompts using the operator's API key or bearer token, including to internal Open WebUI endpoints.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a parameter injection vulnerability in its ClickHouse driver that allows attackers to inject ClickHouse HTTP query parameters through an unencoded db GET parameter. Attackers can lure a logged-in victim into opening a crafted GET link that injects a query parameter, bypassing the POST-only CSRF token. ClickHouse then executes attacker-chosen SQL under the victim's credentials to read, modify, or drop data.

phpMyFAQ 4.1.9 before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an account enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to identify valid logins through differing POST /api/webauthn/prepare responses. Attackers can submit wordlists of usernames, reusing one unconsumed CSRF token without rate limiting, to discover administrator logins for password spraying and phishing.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows FAQ_EDIT users to bypass SvgSanitizer using namespace-prefixed elements like <x:script>. Attackers can upload malicious SVGs through the admin image upload so script runs in the site origin on IIS, hijacking sessions of users like super-admins.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the ClickHouse driver that allows remote attackers to log in to passwordless accounts without the configured defaultPasswordHash password. Attackers who know the name of a ClickHouse no_password account can submit any non-empty password, because connect() skips openPasswordless(), and obtain a session with that account's rights.

phpMyFAQ 4.1.9 before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in multisite deployments that allows attackers to overwrite passkeys of accounts on other tenants via a shared PHP session store. Attackers can run WebAuthn prepare() for a login on one tenant, then replay the session against /api/webauthn/register on another tenant or the master to replace that user's passkeys and log in as admin.

phpMyFAQ 4.1.9 before 4.1.12 and 4.2.0-alpha before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows attackers holding a hijacked session to enroll passkeys using only the session and webauthn CSRF token. Attackers can call /api/webauthn/prepare and /api/webauthn/register to replace the owner's passkeys, gaining persistent passwordless login that survives password changes and resets.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows database users to inject markup by creating FULLTEXT indexes with crafted names. Attackers with CREATE, ALTER or INDEX rights can store markup rendered unescaped in the selection search form, enabling meta refresh redirects, content spoofing and form tampering against other users.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows remote attackers to inject SQL by supplying crafted IN and NOT IN search values that process_length() passes unescaped. Attackers can send a logged-in user a cross-site GET link using a backslash-escaped apostrophe to run blind SQL with that user's database rights on PostgreSQL, SQLite, MS SQL, Oracle, or MySQL in NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES mode.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in DELETE /admin/api/faq/delete that lets language-scoped FAQ_DELETE admins bypass their language scope. Attackers can submit a faqId with an in-scope faqLanguage lacking a translation to wipe shared ACL, tags, votes, comments, and attachments of other translations.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains a filter injection vulnerability in its MongoDB driver that allows attackers to affect other documents by embedding ' AND ' or ') OR (' delimiters in a string _id or searched value. Attackers who can store a crafted document can cause a victim's delete or edit to match unintended documents, deleting the entire collection or modifying another document.

phpMyFAQ from 4.2.0-alpha.2 before 4.2.0-RC.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows language-scoped editors to read other translations by checking FAQ_EDIT against the route language but loading the ?lang= UI-language row. Attackers can request the admin.faq.edit route with an authorized language and a different lang parameter to read drafts, private notes, author e-mails and revisions.

AdminNeo before 5.9.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in OtpLoginPlugin that allows attackers knowing the database password to skip TOTP verification by abusing the permanent-login cookie. Attackers can submit a login with a wrong OTP and permanent=1 to obtain a neo_permanent cookie, then replay it to gain full authenticated database access.

The Soledad theme for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in versions up to, and including, 8.7.7 The public penci_more_post_ajax AJAX action feeds infeedads[ads_code] (base64+urldecoded) to penci_safe_shortcode(), whose allowlist regex inspects only the hyphen-truncated outer shortcode name (e.g. 'adinserter') and never the nested [elementor-element k=.. data=..] tag, so do_shortcode() renders an attacker-chosen Elementor element. The rendered penci-featured-sliders widget passes its unsanitized 'style' setting to include dirname(__FILE__)."/{$style}.php", a path-traversal local file inclusion.

Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester.

This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited.

Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.

Weblate 2026.11 through 2026.11.2 contains a time-of-check time-of-use race condition in the GET /api/tasks/{pk}/ endpoint that exposes unredacted repository error messages. Authenticated project members lacking vcs.view permission can poll failing repository tasks to obtain RepositoryCommandError text revealing upstream repository URLs, filesystem paths, and host names.

Rootways Authorize.net CIM Pro extension for Magento 2 before 4.1.5 contains an unauthenticated server-side request forgery vulnerability in the Apple Pay merchant validation controller. Attackers can supply file://, gopher://, or dict:// URLs in the validationUrl parameter to read app/etc/env.php credentials and encryption keys or reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

affectedData.product: Authorize.net CIM Pro extension for Magento 2

descriptions.value: Xibo CMS before 4.5.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other DataSets' RSS feeds by pairing their own DataSet id with a foreign RSS id. Attackers with dataset.modify permission can read, edit, or delete feeds and steal PSKs, then use the unauthenticated /rss/{psk} endpoint to exfiltrate victim DataSet rows.

Emitter through 3.1 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows any channel key holder to forge a master key because channel keys use bare XOR Salsa20 encryption without a MAC or signature. Attackers can flip the permissions byte to the master value and present the forged key to the keygen service to mint keys with arbitrary permissions on every channel of the contract.

react-native-webview 11.25.1 through 17.1.0 on Android contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows web content to crash the host application via malformed Content-Disposition headers. Attackers can serve a download whose filename* parameter has invalid percent-encoding, triggering an uncaught IllegalArgumentException in URLUtil.parseContentDisposition on the main thread to terminate the app.

Scalar scalar-ninja 0.1.0 before 0.3.3 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in get_scalar_api_reference() that embeds unescaped OpenAPI content inside an inline script element. Attackers can supply an OpenAPI document containing a </script><script> sequence in content or sources to execute scripts in the documentation origin for every user viewing the API reference.

Scalar scalar-ninja 0.1.0 before 0.3.3 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject scripts by supplying unescaped ScalarConfig title values. Attackers controlling title metadata can close the title element with </title> and inject a script tag that executes in the documentation origin for API reference visitors.

Flowise through 3.1.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to reach internal services by exploiting unpinned DNS validation in checkDenyList(). Attackers can configure a chatflow with Playwright or Puppeteer loaders using a DNS-rebinding domain so headless Chromium fetches internal or cloud metadata endpoints, returning responses as document content.

WP File Manager before 8.0.7 contains a file upload restriction bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to upload arbitrary PHP files by exploiting a misconfigured elFinder connector in file_folder_manager.php where an empty uploadDeny list causes allowPutMime() to unconditionally return true, bypassing the uploadAllow restriction. Attackers can upload a .php file directly or upload it under an allowed filename and then rename it via the rename connector command, achieving remote code execution as the web server user.

GPAC 26.02.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in dasher_configure_pid() in src/filters/dasher.c that dereferences ds2->set without checking for NULL. Attackers can supply a crafted MPEG-2 TS file processed with MP4Box -dash to disconnect a PID and crash MP4Box, causing denial of service.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an uninitialized pointer access vulnerability in GetESD() in src/isomedia/track.c that allows attackers to trigger invalid memory reads via crafted MP4 files. Attackers can supply an MP4 with an rvcc box having predefined_rvc_config set to 0 and no meta item index, causing strcmp() on an uninitialized mime_type pointer and crashing MP4Box -add.

GPAC before 26.02.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in gf_filter_pid_set_args_internal() that leaves a stale pointer after gf_props_reset_single() frees a parsed PID property value. Attackers can supply a crafted filelist input processed by MP4Box with -add, causing gf_props_del_property() to access freed memory and crash the application.

Camunda 7.24.0 before 7.24.14 and 7.23.0 before 7.23.17 contains an XML External Entity (XXE) injection vulnerability in the camunda-external-task-client's DomXmlDataFormat.defaultDocumentBuilderFactory(), which fails to disable external entity resolution when parsing object variables serialized with application/xml. An attacker able to write a process variable can trigger arbitrary file read and out-of-band outbound HTTP requests from every worker JVM that deserializes the variable, enabling exfiltration of credentials, service-account tokens, and private key material from network segments deeper than the engine itself.

The ICRTouch white-label TouchTakeaway Cordova applications do not implement certificate or public-key pinning for backend HTTPS connections. The applications therefore rely exclusively on the device’s system trust store when validating server certificates.
An attacker who can cause a device to trust an attacker-controlled certificate authority, or who operates through a compromised or improperly issued trusted certificate, may be able to intercept and modify application traffic.

Due to a Debian-specific patch, the directory used to share data between the
LightDM and the users logging in was writable by the lightdm user of the
unprivileged greeter process. A process running under the lightdm identity
could leverage write access to that directory to force the LightDM process
(running as root) to change ownership and permissions on other root-owned
directories and escalate privileges from the lightdm user to root.

Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320, a registered user can supply path traversal sequences in the hash field accepted by POST /api/attachments/signature when the default local storage provider is in use. In apps/nestjs-backend/src/features/attachments/plugins/local.ts, LocalStorage.presigned uses the client-controlled hash as the storage filename, and LocalStorage.save resolves that path and copies the uploaded request body without calling assertPathWithinStorage on the write path. The read path uses the jail, but the write path does not, allowing the resolved destination to escape the configured storage directory. Because the backend container runs as uid 0, the attacker can write or overwrite arbitrary root-owned files, which can corrupt the instance or lead to root code execution. Object-storage deployments that do not use LocalStorage.save are not affected by this sink. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320.

code16 Sharp is a Laravel-based framework for building content-management and administrative interfaces. Prior to 9.23.0, an authenticated attacker can submit an arbitrary PHP class name through the embed_key parameter to multiple embed API endpoints. The application passes the selected class to the Laravel service container, which invokes the class's __construct() method and recursively instantiates constructor dependencies, potentially causing unauthorized integrity or availability effects. The attacker cannot supply constructor parameter values or invoke an arbitrary method. This issue is fixed in version 9.23.0.

Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264, the routes for PluginService::regenerateSecret and PluginService::delete carry no @Permissions decorator, and the methods omit plugin ownership checks. An authenticated attacker can directly target another plugin's identifier to rotate and disclose its OAuth secret or delete the plugin, including system plugins. Separately, PermissionGuard authorizes several nested API requests using a caller-controlled parent tableId, baseId, or spaceId, while the services resolve the requested child object only by its globally unique identifier. An authenticated attacker can provide a parent resource the attacker owns together with a victim's child identifier. ViewService::getViewById can then disclose another tenant's view configuration, embedded filter values, field layout, and shareId. DashboardService::updatePluginStorage and the view-position updatePluginStorage path can overwrite another tenant's plugin storage because the plugin installation is not rebound to the authorized base, dashboard, table, or view. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264.

libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 17.0.0, the @libp2p/gossipsub default configuration allows a connected remote peer to submit unsigned subscription RPC metadata for arbitrarily many distinct topic strings. handleReceivedSubscription in packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts creates a persistent topics-map entry for each accepted topic, while allowedTopics is unset by default, decodeRpc maxSubscriptions limits only one RPC rather than aggregate topic bytes, and peer scoring has no subscription-volume penalty. A single peer can therefore grow the topics map and committed heap toward out-of-memory conditions, and disconnecting additionally causes removePeer to scan all accumulated topic entries. This issue is fixed in version 17.0.0.

ZoneMinder is a free, open source closed-circuit television software application. Prior to 1.38.4, any authenticated user can use the /api/configs/edit/{name}.json endpoint to modify protected configuration settings because ConfigsController::edit() does not enforce the System=Edit authorization requirement and its system-variable protection is ineffective. An attacker can set ZM_PATH_FFMPEG to a command-bearing value and trigger an exec() sink in web/views/image.php or web/includes/Event.php by requesting frame extraction. This permits arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the web server user and can expose private camera feeds, recordings, and database data or establish persistence. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.4.

Filament Curator is a media picker plugin for Filament panels. From 3.0.0 until 3.7.9, 4.1.2, and 5.1.2, the Curator media panel accepts image/svg+xml files by default and stores and serves their markup inline without sanitization. An authenticated user with media-upload permission can store an SVG containing scripts, event-handler attributes, or javascript: URIs. When another panel user selects the View action, the SVG opens as a top-level browser document and its active content executes in the Filament application's origin. The script can perform authenticated same-origin actions as the viewing user and read same-origin data and script-accessible tokens. Panel thumbnails are not affected because they render through an image element that does not execute SVG script. This issue is fixed in versions 3.7.9, 4.1.2, and 5.1.2.

Rucio is a scientific data management framework. From 1.14.0 until 35.9.1, 38.6.1, 40.4.2, and 41.1.1, validate_auth_token in lib/rucio/core/authentication.py does not distinguish short-lived SSH challenge nonces from authentication tokens stored in the same token table. An unauthenticated attacker can request /auth/ssh_challenge_token for an arbitrary account by supplying X-Rucio-Account, then present the returned X-Rucio-SSH-Challenge-Token as X-Rucio-Auth-Token to authenticate to other API endpoints as that account, including an administrative account. This issue is fixed in versions 35.9.1, 38.6.1, 40.4.2, and 41.1.1.

tiny-secp256k1 is a tiny secp256k1 native/JS wrapper. From 2.1.0 until 2.2.5 for tiny-secp256k1 and from 2.2.2 until 2.2.5 for @bitcoin-js/tiny-secp256k1-asmjs, the three-argument xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck path ignores the backend failure return from xOnlyPointAddTweak when a tweak produces the point at infinity. The shared X_ONLY_PUBLIC_KEY_INPUT buffer then still contains the original point, so a caller-controlled resultToCheck equal to that point can make the stale-buffer comparison return true even though no tweaked key exists. Protocols that rely on this helper to validate caller-controlled internal keys, tweaks, and comparison values can accept an invalid derived key. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.5.

libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 5.1.22, the @libp2p/crypto code reached by the default Identify service accepts a remote peer’s crafted publicKey before peer-id or signature verification and passes it through publicKeyFromProtobuf to the ASN.1 DER decoder. readLength in packages/crypto/src/keys/rsa/der.ts accepts long-form element lengths larger than the remaining buffer, causing readInteger and related readers to loop synchronously over an attacker-claimed length from a very small key blob. Because decoding occurs in one event-loop tick before the remotePeer equality check in packages/protocol-identify/src/identify.ts, the Identify timeout cannot interrupt it, allowing repeated unauthenticated connections to stall all timers and peers and transiently exhaust memory. This issue is fixed in version 5.1.22.

Forge, also called node-forge, is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.1, publicKey.verify() with the default RSASSA-PKCS1-V1_5 scheme in lib/rsa.js parses the recovered DigestInfo with the lenient BER parser asn1.fromDer() and validates its structure with digestInfoValidator without requiring canonical DER bytes. Non-minimal or indefinite lengths, malformed parameter values, and non-canonical object identifier encodings with padded subidentifiers or trailing bytes can leave attacker-controlled data inside an accepted DigestInfo. When the verifying RSA public key uses a low exponent such as e=3, an attacker can use that encoding slack to forge a signature without the private key. The same path is used by X.509 certificate and PKCS#7 signature verification. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.1.

FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, after FreeSWITCH has learned and closed source learning for an RTP peer, read_rtp_packet() and rtp_common_read() in src/switch_rtp.c reject RTP from an unrecognized source only after packet classification and, for encrypted calls, SRTP processing. An unauthenticated attacker with UDP reachability to an active RTP or SRTP media port can sustain a foreign-source packet flood that occupies the media read path and prevents legitimate media from entering FreeSWITCH on calls that consume incoming media for relay or echo. The resulting one-way audio allows the affected endpoint to continue hearing the other party, but the other party loses that endpoint's audio, leaving SIP signaling established while the call is unusable for conversation. Transmit-only playback was unaffected in testing. A caller can learn the media port from the SDP answer, while a third party must first discover an active port, and no valid SRTP key is required. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

Effect is a TypeScript framework that consists of several packages that work together to help build TypeScript applications. Prior to 3.22.1, Schema.TemplateLiteral schemas containing at least two Schema.String spans compile each span to the ambiguous lazy wildcard [\s\S]*?. Decoding a non-matching untrusted string causes cubic regular expression backtracking, which can block the JavaScript event loop. The issue affects Schema.decodeUnknown, Schema.decodeUnknownSync, Schema.is, and consumers such as HttpApi and @effect/rpc payload decoding. This issue is fixed in version 3.22.1.

fzf is a command-line fuzzy finder. Prior to 0.74.5, trigger-driven zsh completion in shell/completion.zsh uses _fzf_feed_fifo to create a FIFO at the predictable shared path ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fzf-complete-fifo-$$ and continues after removal or creation errors. On a multi-user host, a local attacker can pre-create that path as a symlink so the victim's completion stream overwrites a victim-writable file, potentially enabling code execution when that file is later sourced. A pre-created FIFO can instead disclose a bounded stream of completion candidates or block completion. On default modern hosts, fs.protected_symlinks blocks the overwrite variant, and protected_fifos and protected_regular further limit the FIFO disclosure and blocking variants, so exploitation depends on the relevant kernel protections being disabled and on the victim invoking the affected completion. This issue is fixed in version 0.74.5.

HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, the unauthenticated GET /swagger/doc.json endpoint copies the client-supplied X-Forwarded-Host header into the OpenAPI host field without requiring a trusted proxy or validating the value. An attacker can therefore make the served OpenAPI document direct Swagger UI Try it out requests to an attacker-controlled host. When a shared cache or CDN stores and serves that poisoned document to an authenticated user, Swagger UI sends the user's API requests and bearer token to the attacker, enabling disclosure and modification of the user's HomeBox data. Without a shared cache, the attacker can affect only the attacker's own response. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.

HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, a HomeBox password change revokes the user's other session tokens but does not revoke the user's API keys, and API keys have no default API-key expiration. An attacker who has obtained an API key can therefore retain full API-level access after the account owner changes the password and can keep that access indefinitely unless the owner discovers and manually deletes the key by ID. Because the password change terminates other sessions, the surviving API credential can evade the owner's expected containment and detection. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.

WPS Limit Login (wps-limit-login) before 1.5.9.5 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass login lockout protections by keying the per-attempt login counter and lockout map on the raw, non-canonicalized IPv6 client address. Attackers controlling a routable IPv6 /64 prefix can send each login attempt from a fresh address within that range, preventing any counter from reaching the lockout threshold and enabling effectively unlimited brute-force password guessing against WordPress accounts.

gosaml2 is a Pure Go implementation of SAML 2.0. Prior to 0.12.0, ValidateEncodedResponse() calls decryptAssertions() on an EncryptedAssertion before signature or content validation completes, and EncryptedAssertion.DecryptBytes() in types/encrypted_assertion.go slices decoded ciphertext without first validating the required nonce or initialization-vector length. A CipherValue shorter than the 12-byte AES-GCM nonce causes a slice-bounds panic, and an empty AES-CBC CipherValue passes the modulo block-size check before causing a slice-bounds panic at the 16-byte initialization-vector split. An attacker needs only the service provider's public certificate to wrap a symmetric key, and no valid identity-provider signature or relationship is required.
